title: Efficient catalytic degradation of methyl orange from dye wastewater by PANA‐FeMOF and its optimization using the central composite design‐response surface methodology
content:
Abstract

A hydrolyzed polyacrylonitrile fiber-supported FeMOF catalyst (PANA-FeMOF) was utilized as a heterogeneous Fenton catalyst to effectively degrade methyl orange (MO). Central composite design-response surface methodology (CCD-RSM) was employed to optimize four key parameters: pH, degradation time, catalyst dosage, and H2O2 concentration. The study revealed pH as the most influential factor, with optimal conditions identified at pH 3.1, 96.3 min, 0.39 g catalyst, and 0.15 mol/L H2O2 according to the model. These conditions resulted in a notable degradation efficiency of 97.6%, closely matching the predicted value of 97.8%. This research highlights the potential of PANA-FeMOF as an economical and scalable solution for treating dye wastewater.
